title: Monopoles, Center Vortices, Confinement in (3+1)d, and the Lens-Space Twisted Partition Function
abstract: We propose the gauge-invariant criteria of center-vortex condensation and monopole condensation using the $\mathbb{Z}_N^{[1]}$-symmetry twisted partition functions: The torus twisted partition function characterizes the center-vortex condensation, and the lens-space twisted partition function characterizes the monopole condensation. To justify our proposal, we study how these twisted partition functions behave in the adjoint Higgs phase and show that their leading nontrivial contributions come from the center vortex and monopole, respectively. Using the techniques of topological field theories, we uncover the relation between the center-vortex and monopole condensations, and in particular, we prove that the gapped phase with the center-vortex condensation necessarily shows the monopole condensation, too. We then study a center-vortex model with monopoles as an illustrative example, and the higher-charge monopole condensation gives an example of the symmetry fractionalization, which goes beyond the conventional Wilson-'t Hooft classification.
summary: This theoretical work develops gauge-invariant criteria to distinguish and relate center-vortex condensation and monopole condensation in $(3+1)$D Yang-Mills theory using twisted partition functions on specific manifolds. The core achievement is proving that these two distinct topological phenomena are mathematically linked, suggesting a unified understanding of confinement mechanisms.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish gauge-invariant criteria for identifying center-vortex condensation and monopole condensation in $(3+1)$ dimensional Yang-Mills theories.
main_result: It proves a deep relationship showing that the gapped phase exhibiting center-vortex condensation necessarily implies the presence of monopole condensation, linking these two confinement mechanisms.
method: The analysis heavily relies on using $\mathbb{Z}_N$-symmetry twisted partition functions calculated on specific 4-manifolds like the torus ($T^4$) and lens spaces ($L(qN; 1) 	imes S^1$).
model_or_system: The primary model is SU(N) Yang-Mills theory, often studied in the context of an adjoint Higgs phase. The mathematical tools involve topological field theories (TQFTs) and analyzing partition function ratios on compactified spaces.
key_observables: The ratio of twisted partition functions $\mathcal{Z}[B]/\mathcal{Z}[0]$ serves as the diagnostic for condensation; other observables include Wilson loops and inter-quark potentials.
important_parameters: The gauge group rank $N$, the background flux parameters ($q, N$), and the assumption of a non-zero mass gap (gapped phase).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include locality, finiteness of the relevant Hilbert space dimension in the TQFT limit, and the existence of a mass gap for the equivalence theorems to hold.
